note: Extracted 13 September 2026 from a hand-adjudicated PubMed census of 50 records (ipamorelin-pubmed-2026-09), eleven journal abstracts (SRC-072, SRC-076 to SRC-085) and all five practitioner sources. Seeds, the Peptide Handbook, the cheat sheet and Hack Smith are cited by file page; Campbell by the book's page numbers. Regimens that combine ipamorelin with modified GRF (1-29) as a single preparation are recorded once, on the modified GRF (1-29) record, and referenced here in combinations rather than duplicated. Amounts appear only in protocol fields.

compound.shortDescription: A five-amino-acid ghrelin-receptor agonist designed to release growth hormone selectively. Given to people intravenously in two studies; the injected-under-the-skin use practitioner books describe has not been studied in people.
compound.simpleSummary:
Ipamorelin is a small lab-made peptide that switches on the ghrelin receptor, one of the signals that tells the pituitary gland to release growth hormone. It was developed by a pharmaceutical company in the 1990s because, in pigs, it released growth hormone without also raising stress hormones, which similar peptides did.

**It has been given to people twice in published studies, both times into a vein.** In healthy men it caused a short burst of growth hormone and was cleared from the blood within hours. In a trial after bowel surgery it was well tolerated but did not speed up recovery compared with placebo.

**The way it is usually described being used has not been studied in people.** Practitioner books describe injections under the skin one to three times a day, often combined with another peptide, for fat loss, muscle and sleep. No study in people tested any of that. In mice, repeated ipamorelin increased body fat and food intake. Seized black-market products have contained a slightly altered version of the peptide.
compound.practitionerSummary: Ipamorelin (NNC 26-0161; Aib-His-D-2-Nal-D-Phe-Lys-NH2) is a pentapeptide GH secretagogue acting through the GHRP (ghrelin) receptor. In the developer's pharmacology it matched GHRP-6 for GH release in rat pituitary cells, anaesthetised rats and conscious swine, and in swine did not raise ACTH or cortisol above GHRH-stimulated levels even at more than 200 times the GH ED50, nor alter FSH, LH, prolactin or TSH. In healthy men, 15-minute intravenous infusions across five dose levels gave dose-proportional pharmacokinetics, a terminal half-life of about 2 hours and a single GH episode peaking at about 40 minutes. A multicentre phase 2 RCT of intravenous ipamorelin twice daily after bowel resection (n = 114) found it well tolerated with no significant effect on time to tolerated meal or secondary endpoints. Animal work: dose-dependent longitudinal bone growth in rats (subcutaneous, three times daily), preservation of muscle strength and bone formation under glucocorticoid treatment, increased relative body fat and food intake in mice (twice daily, GH-independent), and roughly 20% intranasal bioavailability in rats. Anti-doping laboratories have identified N-terminally glycine-extended ipamorelin in black-market and seized products. No human study of subcutaneous administration, of body composition, or of the combination with a GHRH analogue was identified.
compound.unknownsSummary: Not established in people: the pharmacokinetics and effects of subcutaneous ipamorelin; whether its hormonal selectivity seen in swine holds in humans; any effect on body composition, sleep or recovery; the effect of combining it with a GHRH analogue; long-term safety, including appetite and body fat given the mouse findings; and the identity of products sold under the name.

aliases.note: A salt form named in some studies; the peptide is the same.

compound.molecularDescription: Pentapeptide Aib-His-D-2-Nal-D-Phe-Lys-NH2. Contains non-standard residues (aminoisobutyric acid, D-2-naphthylalanine), so no one-letter sequence is recorded.
compound.nomenclatureNote: One practitioner book calls ipamorelin a growth-hormone-releasing peptide in one chapter and a growth-hormone-releasing hormone in another, swapping it with tesamorelin; the pharmacology places it at the GHRP (ghrelin) receptor. Glycine-extended ipamorelin found in black-market products is a different molecule.

claims.claimText: Ipamorelin is a pentapeptide (Aib-His-D-2-Nal-D-Phe-Lys-NH2) that releases GH through the GHRP receptor with potency and efficacy similar to GHRP-6 in rat pituitary cells, anaesthetised rats and conscious swine; in swine it did not raise ACTH or cortisol above GHRH-stimulated levels even at more than 200 times the dose for half-maximal GH release, and did not change FSH, LH, prolactin or TSH.
claims.plainLanguageText: Ipamorelin releases growth hormone through the ghrelin receptor. In pigs it did this without raising stress hormones.
claims.interpretationNotes: The origin of the selectivity claim every practitioner source repeats. It was shown in pigs.
claims.uncertaintyText: Animal pharmacology from the developer. Human hormonal selectivity was not measured in any record held.

evidence.interpretation: GH release from rat pituitary cells and receptor profiling with antagonists.
evidence.primaryTraceNote: The cited source is the research itself, held at abstract level: design, setting and size are reliable at this depth and the detail of how outcomes were collected is not.

evidence.interpretation: GH, ACTH, cortisol and other pituitary hormones in rats and swine.
evidence.primaryTraceNote: The cited source is the research itself, held at abstract level: design, setting and size are reliable at this depth and the detail of how outcomes were collected is not.

claims.claimText: In healthy men given 15-minute intravenous infusions at five dose levels, ipamorelin showed dose-proportional pharmacokinetics with a terminal half-life of about 2 hours, and produced a single episode of GH release peaking at about 40 minutes and falling to negligible levels.
claims.plainLanguageText: Given into a vein, ipamorelin caused one short burst of growth hormone and was cleared within hours.
claims.interpretationNotes: The only human pharmacokinetic study. The half-life practitioner sources quote matches it, but they describe injection under the skin, which this study did not test.
claims.uncertaintyText: Intravenous, single infusions, healthy men only.

evidence.interpretation: Dose-escalation PK/PD in healthy male volunteers.
evidence.primaryTraceNote: The cited source is the research itself, held at abstract level: design, setting and size are reliable at this depth and the detail of how outcomes were collected is not.

claims.claimText: In a multicentre phase 2 randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial after bowel resection, intravenous ipamorelin twice daily for up to 7 days was well tolerated, and time to first tolerated meal did not differ significantly from placebo, nor did secondary efficacy measures.
claims.plainLanguageText: In a trial after bowel surgery, ipamorelin was well tolerated but did not speed recovery compared with placebo.
claims.interpretationNotes: The only controlled efficacy trial in people, and a negative one. Rat models of the same condition were positive.
claims.uncertaintyText: A small proof-of-concept study with a broad range of underlying conditions.

evidence.interpretation: Tolerability and efficacy endpoints versus placebo (NCT00672074).

claims.claimText: In GH-deficient and GH-intact mice, twice-daily subcutaneous ipamorelin increased body weight modestly, increased fat pad weight relative to body weight and relative body fat on DEXA, and increased food intake and serum leptin, through mechanisms independent of GH.
claims.plainLanguageText: In mice, repeated ipamorelin increased body fat and how much they ate.
claims.interpretationNotes: Directly relevant to practitioner framing of ipamorelin as a fat-loss peptide. Mouse findings do not establish what happens in people; neither does the practitioner framing.
claims.uncertaintyText: Mice; not replicated in the held records.

evidence.interpretation: Body fat, food intake and leptin with ipamorelin versus GH.
evidence.primaryTraceNote: The cited source is the research itself, held at abstract level: design, setting and size are reliable at this depth and the detail of how outcomes were collected is not.

claims.claimText: In adult female rats, subcutaneous ipamorelin three times daily dose-dependently increased longitudinal bone growth and body weight without changing total IGF-I; in rats given a glucocorticoid for three months, adding ipamorelin preserved muscle strength and increased periosteal bone formation.
claims.plainLanguageText: In rats, ipamorelin increased bone growth and protected muscle and bone from steroid damage.
claims.interpretationNotes: Two groups in Denmark, one the developer.
claims.uncertaintyText: Rats. No human bone or muscle study was identified.

evidence.interpretation: Longitudinal bone growth, body weight, IGF-I.
evidence.primaryTraceNote: The cited source is the research itself, held at abstract level: design, setting and size are reliable at this depth and the detail of how outcomes were collected is not.

evidence.interpretation: Muscle strength and bone formation with glucocorticoid.

claims.plainLanguageText: Some ipamorelin is absorbed through the nose in rats, and it can be detected in urine after nasal use.
claims.interpretationNotes: Route evidence that no practitioner source held here relies on; recorded for completeness.
claims.uncertaintyText: Rat bioavailability; a single human volunteer for metabolite identification only.

notYetSupported.statement: The pharmacokinetics and effects of subcutaneous ipamorelin in people.
notYetSupported.why: Both human clinical studies used intravenous infusion. Every practitioner source describes subcutaneous injection.
notYetSupported.whatWouldResolveIt: A human pharmacokinetic and GH-response study of subcutaneous ipamorelin.
notYetSupported.researchQuestion: What are the bioavailability, half-life and GH response of subcutaneous ipamorelin in healthy adults?

notYetSupported.statement: Any effect on body composition, sleep or recovery in people.
notYetSupported.why: No human study measured these outcomes. In mice, body fat increased.
notYetSupported.whatWouldResolveIt: A controlled human study with body-composition measurement.
notYetSupported.researchQuestion: Does repeated ipamorelin change fat mass, lean mass or appetite in adults compared with placebo?

notYetSupported.statement: Whether ipamorelin's hormonal selectivity holds in humans.
notYetSupported.why: The absence of ACTH and cortisol release was shown in swine; the human PK/PD abstract reports GH only.
notYetSupported.whatWouldResolveIt: Measurement of ACTH, cortisol and prolactin after ipamorelin in people.
notYetSupported.researchQuestion: Does ipamorelin raise cortisol or prolactin in humans at GH-releasing doses?

notYetSupported.statement: Ipamorelin combined with a GHRH analogue.
notYetSupported.why: The most common practitioner use; no study identified.
notYetSupported.whatWouldResolveIt: A controlled study of the combination against each component.
notYetSupported.researchQuestion: Does ipamorelin with modified GRF (1-29) or tesamorelin produce a larger GH or IGF-I response than either alone in people?

notYetSupported.statement: Safety of repeated daily use over weeks or months.
notYetSupported.why: The longest human exposure identified is up to 7 days intravenously in hospital.
notYetSupported.whatWouldResolveIt: A longer controlled study with IGF-I, glucose, appetite and adverse-event monitoring.
notYetSupported.researchQuestion: What are the metabolic and appetite effects of eight weeks of daily ipamorelin in adults?

notYetSupported.statement: What products sold as ipamorelin contain.
notYetSupported.why: Glycine-extended ipamorelin has been found in black-market and seized products.
notYetSupported.whatWouldResolveIt: Analysis of purchased products against reference ipamorelin.
notYetSupported.researchQuestion: How often do products sold as ipamorelin contain the reference pentapeptide rather than a modified analogue?

disagreements.topic: Whether ipamorelin affects appetite and body fat.
disagreements.plainLanguageText: Practitioner books say ipamorelin leaves hunger alone and helps fat loss. In mice it increased food intake and body fat. No study in people measured either.
disagreements.explanationNotes: Ipamorelin acts at the ghrelin receptor, the receptor of the body's hunger hormone. The mouse finding and the practitioner claim may both be about different species and settings; neither is a human measurement.
disagreements.resolutionRequirement: A controlled human study measuring appetite, food intake and body composition.

positions.positionText: Does not touch the hunger hormone ghrelin, so hunger is reduced; an excellent choice for fat loss.
Recommended as the best introductory peptide for fat loss.
Increased relative body fat, food intake and leptin in mice, independently of GH.
Describes ipamorelin as a ghrelin-receptor agonist.

disagreements.topic: Whether ipamorelin raises cortisol and prolactin.
disagreements.plainLanguageText: Practitioner books say it does not. That was shown in pigs, not in people.
disagreements.explanationNotes: The practitioner statements are accurate descriptions of the swine result presented without the species.
disagreements.resolutionRequirement: Measurement of ACTH, cortisol and prolactin after ipamorelin in people.

positions.positionText: Does not create prolactin or cortisol.
Does not stimulate cortisol or prolactin release.
In swine, no ACTH or cortisol release beyond GHRH levels, and no change in prolactin.

disagreements.topic: Whether ipamorelin helps the gut recover.
disagreements.plainLanguageText: A practitioner book lists better gut health. Rat studies after surgery were positive. The human trial after bowel surgery found no significant benefit.
disagreements.explanationNotes: The only human test of a gut effect was negative on its key and secondary endpoints; the practitioner claim is general and cites no study.
disagreements.resolutionRequirement: A larger adequately powered human trial, or a defined human gut outcome in another setting.

positions.positionText: Lists better gut health among its outcomes.
Improved bowel function and food intake after surgery in rats.
No significant difference from placebo in time to tolerated meal or secondary endpoints after bowel resection.

disagreements.topic: Whether ipamorelin is a GHRP or a GHRH.
disagreements.plainLanguageText: One practitioner book calls ipamorelin a growth-hormone-releasing peptide in one chapter and a growth-hormone-releasing hormone in another.
disagreements.explanationNotes: The later chapter swaps ipamorelin and tesamorelin. The developer's receptor profiling places ipamorelin at the GHRP receptor, and tesamorelin is a GHRH analogue.
disagreements.resolutionBasis: The developer's pharmacology (SRC-076) shows ipamorelin acts via a GHRP-like receptor, blocked by GHRP and not GHRH antagonists; the same book (SRC-003 p. 58) correctly calls it a GHRP.

positions.positionText: Ipamorelin is a GHRH and tesamorelin a GHRP.
Stimulates GH release via a GHRP-like receptor, shown with GHRP and GHRH antagonists.

disagreements.plainLanguageText: Practitioner sources range from once before bed to three times a day, some in eight-week cycles.
disagreements.explanationNotes: A 2-hour intravenous half-life is consistent with more than one daily dose, but no source cites a study for its schedule and no study examined any of them.
disagreements.resolutionRequirement: A human study of subcutaneous dosing frequency.

positions.positionText: One to three times a day, cycled for no more than 8 weeks.
One to three times daily, fasted.
Morning or evening, five days on and two off, in eight-week cycles.
Terminal half-life about 2 hours after intravenous infusion.

replication.finding: Ipamorelin releases GH without raising ACTH or cortisol.
replication.basis: The developer's pharmacology paper; not repeated in the held records, and not measured in people.

replication.finding: Ipamorelin increases body weight and bone measures in rats.
replication.models: Adult female rats; rats given glucocorticoid.
replication.basis: Novo Nordisk (Denmark, 1999), Sahlgrenska University Hospital (Sweden, 2000) and Aarhus University (Denmark, 2001), no shared institution. The Swedish study found bone mineral content rose in proportion to body weight rather than independently of it.
replication.limitations: The findings overlap rather than match: bone growth, mineral content scaled to weight, and protection under glucocorticoid are different measures.

replication.finding: Ipamorelin speeds gut recovery after abdominal surgery.
replication.basis: Positive in a rat model (University of Oklahoma, 2009); not significant in a multicentre human phase 2 trial (2014).
replication.limitations: The human trial was small and heterogeneous.

replication.finding: Effects of subcutaneous ipamorelin in people.
